clue.text: Supports British artist beginning to shine

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so 'beginning to shine' asks for the S that opens it

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
RA = Royal Academician, crosswordland's usual artist

explanation.surface: A British painter is just starting to make a name for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' reads as a verb about helping the artist, but it is a plural noun for a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym by function: the garment is named for the support it gives.

clue.text: Nasty bloke, foremost of boasters – less serious with it

indicators.note: the foremost letter of a word is the one standing at its front
'with' joins the second piece to the first, and 'it' points back at that first letter

blocks.note: as in a mood that is less heavy

explanation.surface: A boastful, flippant man is being written off as a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTER is mild, rather old-fashioned British slang for an annoying or contemptible man.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: British slang for a contemptible or irritating man, so 'nasty bloke' is a fair gloss.

clue.text: Dane disturbed woman

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are knocked out of their resting order

explanation.surface: A Danish man has upset a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often clue a first name with a bare 'woman' or 'man', so expect a name whenever the definition is that vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a woman's first name stands for any woman, a loose but standard crossword convention.

clue.text: Odd, heartless ally is changing – to become this?

definitions.text: Odd, heartless ally is changing – to become this?

indicators.note: a heartless word has its middle, its heart, cut out
letters that are changing will not stay in the order given

explanation.surface: A friend is strangely turning, and you wonder whether they are about to betray you.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read plainly, an ally who changes sides has turned traitor, and the question mark flags that the definition is the story rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes an ally switching sides, which is exactly what being false to an alliance means.

clue.text: Black suit

blocks.note: the surface wants a colour of cloth; the setter means the colour a card suit is printed in
not a jacket and trousers but one of the four families in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A dark outfit for a formal occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue wants you in a tailor's shop; the suit is in a pack of cards, where two of the four suits, clubs and spades, are black.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: 'suit' shifts from clothing to cards, and spades is one of the two suits printed in black.

clue.text: Favouring someone starting something less superficial

blocks.note: in favour of, as in pros and cons
the person who starts a business or society

explanation.surface: A preference for whoever gets a project off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' tempts you to take a first letter; here it is part of the description of the person who sets something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means deep, the opposite of superficial, so the comparative, more profound, is less superficial.

clue.text: Drink, one given to a Shakespearean character

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A glass of something handed to an actor playing a Shakespeare role.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroine of The Merchant of Venice, who argues 'the quality of mercy' in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: she is one of Shakespeare's best-known heroines, so the general term covers her.

clue.text: Exploited? That’s not new

blocks.note: second-hand, as a car on a forecourt

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they were taken advantage of, and gets the weary reply that this is nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like a comment on the first, but it is its own definition: second-hand.
explanation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: to be exploited is to be made use of, and a second-hand item has been owned before.

clue.text: Was in charge with lines put down

blocks.note: like writing paper with its lines drawn across

explanation.surface: A leader who governed while laying down the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines put down' suggests orders being issued; it is the lines drawn on writing paper with a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: governing a country, and paper marked with straight lines using a ruler.

clue.text: Dominating supremo I twice upset

indicators.note: 'twice' tells you to write the I that precedes it two times over
letters that are upset are overturned and land in a new order

blocks.note: the letter I, taken two times

explanation.surface: A domineering boss has been upset twice by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supremo' looks like part of the definition, the dominating boss, but every letter of it goes into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: overbearing and commanding, behaving like an emperor.

clue.text: New design with everything included as indicated

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a rearranged one
what is included is taken inside

explanation.surface: A fresh design with every feature built in, just as specified.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged DESIGN has to split after its fourth letter to take the insert.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to show or point something out by a sign.

clue.text: Corpulent editor doomed

blocks.note: ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An overweight editor is heading for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one tabloid headline, but it splits cleanly into two pieces and a definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both mean destined by fate, usually to something bad.

clue.text: What may provide power for a group of guns

blocks.note: an electric cell for a torch or phone

explanation.surface: Something that supplies the force behind a line of artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence about firepower, which hides that 'for' is just a hinge between two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One word, two senses: a cell storing electric charge, and a set of artillery pieces fired together.

clue.text: Group at church led by bishop

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front, so the bishop's letter comes first

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A congregation gathered at church behind their bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is named last in the clue but 'led by' puts his letter at the front of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a set of things produced or handled together.

clue.text: Africans and I eat in shop newly built

indicators.note: the letters are built again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some Africans and the speaker dine in a brand-new shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly built' reads as describing the shop, but it applies to all the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: people of one African country are Africans.

clue.text: Food item with herb seen around America

indicators.note: the herb is seen wrapped around the other piece

blocks.note: a common kitchen herb, split SA…GE
the United States, set inside the herb

explanation.surface: A dish flavoured with herbs, served across America.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage really is the classic herb in pork bangers, British slang for sausages, so the surface is a recipe as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a link of seasoned minced meat is one item of food.

clue.text: Bird’s home eerily unstable, left to fall apart

indicators.note: unstable letters will not hold their order
left gives L, and letting it fall drops it out
falling apart means the remaining letters come loose and resettle

blocks.note: EERILY with its L taken out

explanation.surface: An eagle's nest perched precariously, about to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not 'abandoned' but the letter L, and it is the one letter of the fodder that does not survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Source of light in vault or chamber

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the words that follow it

explanation.surface: Something to see by inside a crypt or dark room.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a scene you would need the answer for, which makes the hidden word easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: a hand-held lamp, called a flashlight in American English.

clue.text: Drink chum knocked over

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round

explanation.surface: A friend's drink has been spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like a noun, a glass knocked over; it is the verb, as a cat drinks milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for the verb: to drink by scooping with the tongue, as cats and dogs do.

clue.text: Dad with chaps gathered round area for ceremonial events

indicators.note: the chaps gather round the area, holding it inside

blocks.note: A = area, set inside the chaps

explanation.surface: Father and his friends form a circle around a space set aside for ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Area for' looks like the start of the definition; the area is a single letter, and 'for' is only the hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain description: elaborate public spectacles, often processions in costume.

clue.text: Christmas month with gold ornamentation

blocks.note: DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: December's golden decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Christmas tinsel, and the answer really is the decorations; only the pieces are hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the style of furnishing and decoration of a room.

clue.text: Like clique in pub, turning up with discord all around

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from the bottom to the top
the discord surrounds the other piece on every side

blocks.note: a clash = discord, placed around the turned pub

explanation.surface: A cliquey crowd in a pub, rowing among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as the container instruction; it belongs to the surface, and 'all around' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for a closed group: tight-knit and excluding outsiders, as a clique does.

clue.text: Complete lack of faith reported? Keep going!

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is heard, not seen

blocks.note: whole = complete, doubt = lack of faith

explanation.surface: Someone with no faith left at all is urged not to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break moves: said quickly, the D of the second word slides onto the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to hold out is to persist and not give in, here as an exhortation.

clue.text: Find old feline in drained-out lake

indicators.note: the cat goes inside the lake
a drained word has its contents emptied, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: LAKE emptied of its middle, placed around the other pieces

explanation.surface: Searching for an elderly cat in a lake that has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' sits at the front looking like an instruction to the solver; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to discover where something is.

clue.text: The rat, horrible menace

indicators.note: a horrible mess of letters has lost its proper order

explanation.surface: Someone denounces a rat of a man as a nasty menace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' reads as an adjective on the definition, a horrible menace, but it scrambles the rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a person or thing likely to cause harm.

clue.text: Car repair shop filled with black rubbish

indicators.note: the garage has the black poured inside it

blocks.note: where mechanics fix cars, split GAR…AGE
B = black, as on pencils, set inside

explanation.surface: A mechanic's workshop full of dark junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface already paints the answer: a workshop full of junk, so the definition hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, the usual American word for household rubbish.

clue.text: Some idiotic act impedes plants

indicators.note: only some of the letters that follow are used

explanation.surface: A stupid act holds back the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles three words: the last letter of 'idiotic', all of 'act', and the first letter of 'impedes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: spiny succulents are one family of plants.

clue.text: Talk about bowler maybe

indicators.note: 'maybe' says the bowler is only one example of what is wanted

blocks.note: a bowler is a round, hard-crowned kind of headgear

explanation.surface: Discussing a cricket bowler, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a bowler is a cricketer, but here it is the round felt hat; 'about' is not a container but the C of circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to talk informally.

clue.text: Shuffle bottom, then roam

blocks.note: to wander widely, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Wriggle about on your seat, then wander off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' looks like an anagram instruction; it is the definition, and there is no anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as when a deck of cards is put into a new order.

clue.text: King accompanied by one companion wanting for nothing?

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monarch with a single friend lacks nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British order awarded for service to the nation; its letters CH are a crossword standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the wealthy lack nothing money can buy, and the question mark admits it is a description, not a synonym.

clue.text: In house we require vessel for water

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something the household needs for holding water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In house' reads as the setting; 'In' is the instruction and the house supplies only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a large jug, traditionally stood in a washbasin.

clue.text: A non-drinker with aim, worker to become escort

blocks.note: a goal, as in ends and means
the ant is crosswordland's standard worker

explanation.surface: A sober, ambitious labourer sets out to be someone's escort.
explanation.walkthrough: Four short pieces in a row; TT and ANT are conventions worth knowing, and 'to become' only joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone who accompanies and looks after another.

clue.text: Shy English class

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A timid English schoolroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' is not timid but the verb to throw, and 'class' is a social rank, not a school form. A coconut shy is a British fairground stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a hereditary social rank, the Hindu sense widened to any rigid class.
